I have farmed these lands since I was a boy following my father’s footsteps, and I learned that beans grow well enough without chemical fertilizer — they even make the soil better for the maize I plant elsewhere. This plot is rented, not my own, so I will not haul manure here or spend money on shop seed when I have good seed from last season saved in a tin under my bed. My wife and children will help me clear it with the hand hoe, weed it twice when the rains come, and harvest when the pods turn dry. I will not hire workers because paying wages for a half-hectare of beans would leave me with nothing to buy salt and kerosene.
